title: The Great Finger in the Wendy’s Chili Caper
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the 2005 Wendy's chili finger hoax in San Jose, California. Anna Ayala claimed she found a human finger in her chili at a downtown San Jose Wendy's in March 2005. Wendy's and police investigated; supplier checks, polygraphs, and forensic food microscopy by Dr. Lynn Bates of Alteca found the finger had not been cooked for three hours in chili. Investigators uncovered Ayala's history of lawsuits and a trailer sale scam. Ayala and husband Jamie Plasencia were arrested in Las Vegas. A $100,000 tip line led to Mike Casey, whose employee Brian Rossiter had lost a finger in a tailgate accident and reportedly gave it to Plasencia, who owed him money. Ayala was sentenced to nine years and Plasencia to twelve. Wendy's lost about $2.5 million. The episode also covers other false and real fast-food finger incidents and a listener email about Adidas and Puma. Episode is a regular full episode.
topics: Stuff You Should Know true crime

segments.title: Opening banter and tour dates
segments.summary: Hosts promote upcoming live shows in Seattle, Portland and San Francisco and joke about aging, then introduce the Wendy's chili finger story.
topics: Stuff You Should Know live shows

segments.title: The finger in the chili
segments.summary: Anna Ayala says she bit into a human finger in her Wendy's chili at the downtown San Jose location in March 2005. Employees dump the chili, police call it a health department matter, and the story spreads quickly on local and national news.

segments.title: Business impact and police hands-off approach
segments.summary: Wendy's sales drop, especially in the Bay Area. Police treat the case as a health department issue and leave Wendy's to investigate. The company's franchise owners and health inspectors get involved.

segments.title: Wendy's internal investigation and forensics
segments.summary: Wendy's checks employees' hands, gives polygraph tests, and traces chili ingredients to seven suppliers with no finger injuries reported. Dr. Lynn Bates of Alteca finds no sign the finger was cooked in chili for three hours. Wendy's concludes it was being defrauded and brings in a detective.

segments.title: Ayala's litigation history and early tips
segments.summary: The detective finds Ayala filed at least thirteen civil lawsuits, and the hosts discuss several cases including a GM suit and a Taco Bell-style claim. The tip line brings in early tips that Ayala was fleecing Wendy's. Ayala goes on Good Morning America and later tries to drop her lawsuit.

segments.title: Ayala's background, Ken Bono claim, and the trailer scam
segments.summary: Police search Ayala's home and she claims they abused her family. Ken Bono says the finger belonged to a deceased aunt. Investigators uncover a trailer sale scam and Plasencia's child support debt. Sandy Almond's claim about a leopard bite is a red herring, and a Mexico ranch tip also goes nowhere.

segments.title: Arrests and the solved finger identity
segments.summary: Ayala and Plasencia are arrested in Las Vegas around day thirty-two. Wendy's raises its reward to $100,000 and two callers respond. Mike Casey of Lamb Asphalt links the finger to Brian Rossiter, who lost a finger in a tailgate accident and reportedly gave it to Plasencia over a debt. DNA testing confirms the match.

segments.title: Sentencing, losses, and other fast food finger cases
segments.summary: Ayala admits she cooked the finger slightly and that she did not bite it or vomit. She is sentenced to nine years and Plasencia to twelve. Wendy's lost about $2.5 million and was ordered restitution. The hosts list other real and fake fast-food finger incidents, including Arby's, Coal's Frozen Custard and TGI Friday's.

segments.title: Listener mail on Adidas and Puma
segments.summary: A listener shares family connections to Adidas and Herzogenaurach and praises the show's episode on the Dassler brothers. The hosts thank the listener and a teacher who uses the show in class.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close with contact information and an email address for listeners.
